page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the running head and page number at the top. Section numbers XCVIII. and XCIX. stand centred above their paragraphs. No marginal notes. The gathering signature "Kk 4" stands at the foot.

p.i: Ut autem accidit tempore Noe, sic etiam erit adventus filii hominis. Ut enim tempore, quod fuit ante diluvium, comedebatur, potabatur, contrahebantur invicem matrimonia, usq; ad diem quo Noe in arcam ingressus est, nec ante cognitum est quàm venit diluvium, quod omnes sustulit: sic erit etiam adventus filii hominis. Tum ex duobus, qui ruri erunt, alter assumetur, alter relinquetur: ex duabus in pistrino molentibus, altera assumetur, altera relinquetur. Matth 24.

Tertio autem die nuptiæ factæ sunt Cana in Galilæa, ubi & Jesu mater erat. Et Jesus, ejusque discipuli ad nuptias vocati sunt. Cumque defecisset vinum, Jesum mater sic alloquitur: Vinum non habent. Cui Jesus: Quid tum postea?[?] mulier, nondum venit hora mea. Mater ministros monuit, ut quod ille eis jussisset, facerent. Erant illic posita sex lapidea folia, ut ferebat Judæorum purificatio,

page.notes: Line-end hyphens kept: "e-tiam", "contraheban-tur", "molenti-bus", "relinque-tur", "relin-quetur", "lier" (mu-lier). Long s and f in "sustulit", "sex" and "est" are read as long s. Doubtful: "usq;" (the abbreviation mark is hard to read); the mark after "postea" (a question mark or similar glyph, marked [?]). Printed "folia" after "lapidea" looks like a printing error; left as printed. "Matth 24." is set in italic within the paragraph and is treated as text, not a note. The spelling "venit" and "vocati" are copied from the print; the printed "uenit" and "uocati" were normalised to v as the rules require. Ampersand kept as printed.
